product_from_film: Palus Finance offers managed treasury portfolios for startups and businesses, linked to an existing bank account.
explains_well: The founders connect newly raised idle cash to a treasury-management need and state the intended offer in plain language.
unclear: The film gives benefit claims and a comparison chart but no account-linking, portfolio-choice or withdrawal example.
scenario: Founders discuss idle startup cash and existing treasury options, then introduce managed portfolios and an illustrative growth comparison.
product_clear_basis: After naming Palus and benefit claims at 53–60s, the ASR says it is an app connected to the existing bank account; the following script names advisor-run portfolios.

categories.finding: Text communicates idle cash and return claims silently, but bank connection and portfolio management rely more on the script.
Oversized words draw attention strongly, sometimes covering much of the presenter scene. The chart values dominate its fine-print assumptions.
More than half the film passes before the named solution; the chart provides the only sustained visual product-related artifact.
The idle-cash opportunity is answered with managed-portfolio and return claims, not a demonstrated customer setup or usable result.
The founders frame neglected cash as an opportunity and greater control; response is unmeasured.
Idle cash and founder scale stay consistent, though the critique of competitors and chart are not connected to one customer case.

The inspected 71s chart note says Palus uses typical SOFR plus a 1.25% spread, monthly compounding, named comparison funds and returns net of platform advisory fees, with a past-performance warning. These are displayed assumptions, not verified results. Safety, accessibility, fees and up-to-50%-more-yield claims remain untested.
The idle fundraising cash scenario and explicit treasury comparison make the pitch specific; presenter typography itself is generic.
Show how the customer makes the treasury decision.
